title: Automated FP8/INT8 benchmark report generator (tables/plots) + publish to Drive/Confluence
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Context
We’re generating a large FP8/INT8 benchmark matrix (model x GPU x quant mode x runtime commit) and need a repeatable report artifact (tables + plots) that we can:
1) review internally during the sprint,
2) attach to the final sprint report in Confluence,
3) optionally share a sanitized summary with prospects/customers via Solutions.

Right now we have raw artifacts (JSON + parquet stub) and ad-hoc notebooks. We need a deterministic “report generator” that takes a run directory and outputs a standardized report package.

## Goal
Build a small report generator (CLI + templates) that:
- Ingests benchmark-lab result artifacts (JSON metadata + metric series; parquet where present)
- Produces:
  - summary tables (throughput, TTFT/TPOT, p50/p95/p99)
  - deltas vs baseline commit (or tagged baseline run)
  - plots for key metrics (TTFT/TPOT, tokens/sec, scheduler queue wait, phase breakdown)
  - a machine-readable summary JSON for later dashboard ingestion
- Publishes outputs to:
  - Engineering Drive folder (canonical location for the sprint)
  - Confluence page (embedded tables/plots + links to raw artifacts)

## Inputs / Assumptions
- Artifact format from benchmark-lab: see PRs around “results artifact format” and “consistent metadata tags” (GPU SKU, quant mode, runtime commit, workload preset, region)
- Metric definitions/aggregation rules follow ADR: TTFT/TPOT/tokens/sec + aggregation across repetitions
- Report should support both:
  - end-to-end serving benchmarks (streaming chat and non-streaming)
  - microbench kernel runs (where available) as optional sections

## Deliverables
A) `bench report` (or `benchmark-lab report`) CLI that:
- Accepts `--input` (local path or s3 URI), `--baseline` (run id or commit), `--output` dir
- Emits a report bundle:
  - `index.md` (or `report.md`) + `index.html` (optional but preferred)
  - `/plots/*.png` (or svg)
  - `/tables/*.csv` + `/tables/*.md`
  - `summary.json` (topline metrics + deltas + links)

B) Publishing script (can be separate) that:
- Uploads the bundle to Drive in a fixed folder path
- Updates/creates a Confluence page under Serving Runtime > Benchmarking & Perf Suite:
  - Attaches plots
  - Pastes summary tables
  - Links to full bundle and raw run artifacts

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a completed matrix run (>= 1 model family, >= 2 GPUs, FP16+FP8+INT8), the tool generates a report without manual edits.
- Report includes at minimum:
  1) Table: per (model, GPU, quant) with TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost proxy column (if available).
  2) Table: delta vs baseline (%) for TTFT p95, TPOT p95, tokens/sec.
  3) Plot: TTFT p95 by GPU broken out by quant mode.
  4) Plot: TPOT p95 by GPU broken out by quant mode.
  5) Plot: throughput (tokens/sec) by GPU broken out by quant mode.
  6) Section listing anomalies/flags (missing runs, failed correctness guardrail, high variance).
- Publishing produces a stable URL (Drive) and Confluence page link; reruns update the same page (append new run id and keep previous runs linked).

## Non-goals
- Building a fully general BI system (dashboards handled separately in observability pack).
- Customer-facing polished narrative; this is internal-first, deterministic, and reviewable.

## Implementation Notes
- Prefer Python (pandas) for parsing and aggregation; altair/matplotlib for plots.
- Templates: markdown with small Jinja2 templates.
- Keep logic aligned with the metrics ADR (outlier handling, robust stats). Do NOT re-implement aggregation differently from perf-canary comparator.
- Be careful with time zones and run ids; include runtime commit + benchmark-lab commit + container digest in the report header.

## Risks / Open Questions
- Confluence API auth: use existing automation pattern from release notes posting (Connor can point to approach). If blocked, ship Drive-only first.
- Some runs may only have JSON and no parquet; tool must degrade gracefully.
- Baseline selection: prefer explicit `--baseline-run-id` to avoid “moving baseline” confusion.

## Owners / Reviewers
- Owner: Rina Kobayashi
- Reviewer: Noah Patel (metrics sanity), Allison Grant (publishing format + links), Connor O’Brien (Confluence automation / release hygiene)
